q/acne-diet.a: A high glycaemic index diet and, in some people, milk and whey protein are linked with acne.

q/acne-zinc.a: It has moderate evidence and many users report improvement. Take it with food so it does not cause nausea.

q/acv-weight.n: Does apple cider vinegar help weight loss?
q/acv-weight.a: The benefit is very small. Always dilute it, because it damages tooth enamel.

q/afib-alcohol.a: Yes. Abstaining reduced recurrences in a study.

q/alcohol-safe.a: There is no risk-free level. The less the better, with alcohol-free days.

q/alcohol-sleep.a: It helps you fall asleep, but it disrupts deep and REM sleep in the second half of the night.

q/anemia-food.a: Red meat, liver and mussels have well-absorbed iron. Lentils, beans and spinach have less absorbable iron; lemon helps.

q/anxiety-natural.n: Are there natural remedies for anxiety?
q/anxiety-natural.a: Aerobic exercise, sleep, less caffeine, breathing exercises. Lavender oil (Silexan) has the best evidence among supplements.

q/ashwa-safe.a: Usually yes for short-term use, but there are rare reports of liver damage. Not in pregnancy, hyperthyroidism or autoimmune disease.

q/b12-form.a: Both correct deficiency. Cyanocobalamin is the most studied and stable.

q/b12-injection.a: By mouth, 1000–2000 µg a day is usually just as effective. Injections are needed for severe nerve damage or some cases of pernicious anaemia.

q/b12-vegan.n: Do I need B12 if I'm vegan?
q/b12-vegan.a: Yes, always. B12 is not found in a reliable form in plant foods. Spirulina is not a good source.

q/backpain-rest.n: Should I rest or move with low back pain?
q/backpain-rest.a: Staying as active as possible leads to faster recovery than resting.

q/belly-fat.n: How do I lose belly fat?
q/belly-fat.a: Spot reduction does not exist. Overall weight loss, exercise and sleep also reduce belly fat.

q/biotin-hair.a: Only if there is a real deficiency, which is rare. At high doses it distorts tests such as thyroid and troponin.

q/bloating-what.a: Eating slowly, fewer fizzy drinks, testing for lactose intolerance and, with irritable bowel, peppermint oil or a low-FODMAP diet with a dietitian.

q/bp-food.n: What lowers blood pressure without medicines?
q/bp-food.a: Less salt, the DASH diet, weight loss, exercise and less alcohol. Together they can lower systolic pressure by 10–20 mmHg.

q/bread-bad.a: Wholegrain bread in sensible amounts is part of a healthy diet. Large amounts of white bread raise blood sugar quickly.

q/breakfast-must.n: Is breakfast the most important meal?
q/breakfast-must.a: For adults it is not essential. The quality of the overall diet matters more.

q/breastfeeding-supp.n: What do I need while breastfeeding?
q/breastfeeding-supp.a: Keep taking iodine and, for vegan mothers, B12. The baby needs vitamin D drops.

q/burnout-help.a: Boundaries at work, sleep, exercise and support. If it comes with depression, see a specialist.

q/c-cold.n: Does vitamin C help with colds?
q/c-cold.a: Regular intake slightly shortens colds (about 8%) but does not make them less frequent. Started once you are ill, the effect is negligible.

q/c-much.n: Is too much vitamin C dangerous?
q/c-much.a: More than 2 g a day often causes diarrhoea and raises the risk of kidney stones. Care is needed with G6PD deficiency and haemochromatosis.

q/celiac-test.a: With a blood antibody test while you are still eating gluten, confirmed by a biopsy.

q/checkup-what.n: Which tests do I need every year?
q/checkup-what.a: It depends on age and history: blood pressure, lipids, blood sugar, and cancer screening (breast, cervix, bowel) according to guidelines.

q/chemo-antioxidants.n: Can I take antioxidants during chemotherapy?
q/chemo-antioxidants.a: Only with your oncologist's approval. Some may reduce how well the treatment works.

q/cholesterol-food.n: What should I eat to lower cholesterol?
q/cholesterol-food.a: Oats, legumes, nuts, plant sterols, olive oil instead of butter. Together they can lower LDL by up to 20–30%.

q/coffee-good.n: Is coffee good or bad for you?
q/coffee-good.a: For most people, 2–4 cups are linked with lower mortality in observational studies. Take care in pregnancy, with anxiety, arrhythmias and insomnia.

q/coffee-sleep.n: How many hours before bed should I stop coffee?
q/coffee-sleep.a: At least 6–8 hours. Caffeine 6 hours before bed reduced sleep by about 1 hour.

q/cold-shower-work.n: Are cold showers good for you?
q/cold-shower-work.a: One large study showed fewer sick days. Other benefits have little data. Avoid with heart disease.

q/cold-what.n: What should I do when a cold starts?
q/cold-what.a: Rest, fluids, zinc lozenges in the first 24 hours. Fever for more than 3 days or breathlessness need a doctor.

q/collagen-work.n: Does collagen work for the skin?
q/collagen-work.a: Meta-analyses show a small improvement in elasticity and hydration, but many studies are funded by companies. Sunscreen has far stronger evidence.

q/constipation-fast.a: Prunes or kiwis, water, movement. Psyllium and magnesium are gentle options. A lasting change after 50 needs checking.

q/cramps-night.a: Calf stretches before bed. Magnesium helps a few people, mainly in pregnancy. Some medicines (diuretics, statins) cause cramps.

q/creatine-hair.a: One small study showed a rise in DHT, but it did not measure hair loss and has not been confirmed.

q/creatine-loading.n: Do I need a creatine loading phase?
q/creatine-loading.a: No. With 3–5 g a day the muscles fill up in 3–4 weeks. Loading only speeds this up.

q/creatine-safe.a: Yes, for healthy adults at 3–5 g a day, and it is one of the most studied supplements. It slightly raises creatinine in tests without meaning harm. With kidney disease only with a doctor.

q/curcumin-liver.a: Turmeric in food does not. Highly concentrated extracts, especially with piperine, have been linked with rare cases of liver damage.

q/depression-supp.a: EPA-rich omega-3 and saffron have some evidence as an add-on to treatment. Exercise has strong evidence. With antidepressants, never St John's wort or 5-HTP.

q/detox.a: The liver and kidneys clean the body. "Detox" programmes have no evidence and some are dangerous.

q/diarrhea-kids.n: What do I give a child with diarrhoea?
q/diarrhea-kids.a: A rehydration solution from the pharmacy in small, frequent sips, and food when they ask for it. Babies, blood or signs of dehydration: see a doctor.

q/echinacea-work.a: The results are mixed. Possibly a small reduction in colds.

q/eczema-help.a: Emollient creams every day, short lukewarm baths and avoiding fragrances. Evening primrose oil does not help.

q/egg-raw.a: They carry a risk of salmonella and raw egg white binds biotin. Cooked eggs are better.

q/eggs-cholesterol.a: For most people, 1 egg a day does not raise cardiovascular risk. With diabetes or very high LDL, eat them in moderation.

q/elderberry-work.a: Small studies show slightly shorter symptoms. It does not replace the vaccine or antivirals.

q/elderly-supp.a: Vitamin D, B12 and enough protein are needed more often. With many medicines, every addition needs an interaction check.

q/empty-stomach.n: Supplements on an empty stomach or with food?
q/empty-stomach.a: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) and omega-3 with food. Iron is best on an empty stomach if you tolerate it. Zinc with food so it does not cause nausea.

q/endurance-fast.n: How do I improve my endurance quickly?
q/endurance-fast.a: Combine easy aerobic exercise with 1 interval session a week and increase volume gradually. If you smoke, quitting brings quick improvement.

q/energy-drinks-kids.n: Are energy drinks dangerous for teenagers?
q/energy-drinks-kids.a: Yes. A lot of caffeine and sugar, fast heart rate and insomnia. Not for children or teenagers, and never with alcohol.

q/exercise-howmuch.n: How much exercise do I need a week?
q/exercise-howmuch.a: 150–300 minutes of moderate or 75–150 of vigorous aerobic exercise, and 2 days of strength training.

q/exercise-start.n: How do I start exercising from zero?
q/exercise-start.a: Start with a 10-minute walk a day and increase every week. Add 2 days of simple strength exercises. With heart disease or symptoms, see a doctor first.

q/expire.a: They usually lose potency rather than become dangerous. Omega-3 and probiotics do spoil, though: if they smell rancid, throw them away.

q/eyelid-twitch.a: Usually from tiredness, stress or caffeine, and it goes away on its own. If it lasts for weeks or spreads to the face, see a doctor.

q/falls-prevent.n: How do I prevent falls in older adults?
q/falls-prevent.a: Tai chi and balance exercises, a review of medicines and eyesight, good lighting at home.

q/fasting-work.a: You lose as much weight as with simple calorie reduction. It helps people who find it easy.

q/fatburners.a: They have no meaningful benefit and some have caused serious harm. Weight loss comes from diet and movement.

q/fatigue-tests.n: I always feel tired. Which tests should I get?
q/fatigue-tests.a: Full blood count, ferritin, B12, thyroid, blood sugar, vitamin D. Also consider sleep (apnoea), mood and medicines.

q/fatty-liver-diet.n: What should I do about fatty liver?
q/fatty-liver-diet.a: Lose 7–10% of your weight, exercise, less sugar and alcohol. Avoid "detox" herbs.

q/fe-constip.n: Iron makes me constipated. What do I do?
q/fe-constip.a: Try iron bisglycinate, taking it every other day or with a little food. Black stools are expected.

q/fe-everyone.n: Should I take iron if I feel tired?
q/fe-everyone.a: Not without tests. With thalassaemia or haemochromatosis, iron is harmful. Measure ferritin and a full blood count first.

q/fe-howto.n: How should I take iron for better absorption?
q/fe-howto.a: On an empty stomach or with a little food, with vitamin C or an orange, away from coffee, tea, milk and calcium. Taking it every other day increases absorption.

q/fertility-men.a: Quitting smoking, a normal weight, less alcohol, avoiding anabolic steroids. Supplements have limited evidence.

q/fiber-howmuch.n: How much fibre do I need?
q/fiber-howmuch.a: 25–30 g a day. Increase gradually and drink water so you do not get bloated.

q/fish-mercury.n: How much fish should I eat because of mercury?
q/fish-mercury.a: 2 portions a week, mainly small fish (sardines, anchovies). In pregnancy, avoid swordfish and shark.

q/focus-adhd.a: A small benefit in some studies. It does not replace treatment.

q/folic-when.n: When should I start folic acid for pregnancy?
q/folic-when.a: At least 1 month before conception and until week 12, 400 µg a day. With epilepsy, diabetes or a previous pregnancy with a defect, the doctor sets a higher dose.

q/food-intolerance-test.n: Are IgG food intolerance tests worth it?
q/food-intolerance-test.a: No. They have no proven diagnostic value and can lead to unnecessary restrictions.

q/frozen-veg.a: Yes, they keep their nutrients well and are economical.

q/fruit-sugar.n: Does fruit have a lot of sugar?
q/fruit-sugar.a: The sugar in whole fruit comes with fibre. Fruit is linked with less, not more, diabetes.

q/g6pd-favism.n: What should I avoid with favism?
q/g6pd-favism.a: Broad beans, naphthalene (mothballs), certain medicines (there is an official list) and very high doses of vitamin C. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist.

q/gluten-bad.a: No. A gluten-free diet is necessary only with coeliac disease, wheat allergy or confirmed sensitivity.

q/gout-diet.n: What should I avoid with gout?
q/gout-diet.a: Beer and alcohol, drinks with fructose, a lot of red meat and seafood. Water and weight loss help.

q/grapefruit-meds.n: Why is grapefruit not allowed with some medicines?
q/grapefruit-meds.a: It blocks an enzyme in the gut and raises levels of some statins, immunosuppressants and heart medicines. Read the patient leaflet.

q/greentea-liver.n: Is green tea bad for the liver?
q/greentea-liver.a: The drink is not. Extracts in capsules with high EGCG have caused liver damage, especially on an empty stomach.

q/greyhair-reverse.n: Can grey hair turn dark again?
q/greyhair-reverse.a: Rarely, only if caused by a deficiency (e.g. B12). It is usually hereditary.

q/gut-health.n: How do I improve gut health?
q/gut-health.a: A variety of plant foods, fibre, fermented foods. Probiotics help in specific situations.

q/hairloss-women.n: What should I check if my hair is falling out?
q/hairloss-women.a: Ferritin, thyroid, vitamin D and, in women, hormones. After childbirth, fever or stress, hair loss is common and temporary.

q/hangover-cure.a: None proven. Water between drinks, food beforehand, sleep. Do not take paracetamol after a lot of alcohol.

q/headache-water.a: Yes, mild dehydration is linked with headache and worse mood.

q/heart-supp.n: Is there a supplement for the heart?
q/heart-supp.a: None replaces medicines. High-dose EPA helps with high triglycerides under a doctor. Vitamin E and beta-carotene did not help.

q/hiit-age.n: Can I do HIIT at an older age?
q/hiit-age.a: Yes, with adjusted intensity, and after your doctor approves it if you have heart disease.

q/honey-cough.a: Yes, in children over 1 year it reduces night-time coughing. Never give it to babies under 1 year.

q/immune-boost.n: Is there anything that "boosts" the immune system?
q/immune-boost.a: Sleep, exercise, vaccines and correcting deficiencies (D, zinc). "Immune booster" products have no clear evidence.

q/iodine-salt.a: Yes, instead of plain salt, but keep the total amount of salt moderate.

q/jetlag-help.n: How do I deal with jet lag?
q/jetlag-help.a: Daylight at your destination at the right times and melatonin 0.5–3 mg at the destination's bedtime.

q/joint-supp.a: Turmeric has relatively the best evidence for knee osteoarthritis. Glucosamine has mixed results. Weight loss and strengthening help more.

q/juice-fruit.n: Is fresh juice the same as fruit?
q/juice-fruit.a: No. Juice has less fibre and a lot of sugar. Choose the whole fruit.

q/keto-safe.a: For a short time in healthy people usually yes, but it can raise LDL a lot. Not in type 1 diabetes, pregnancy or with certain medicines.

q/kidneystone-water.n: How much water for kidney stones?
q/kidneystone-water.a: Enough to pass more than 2–2.5 litres of urine a day. That usually means 2.5–3 litres of fluids.

q/kids-sleep-melatonin.n: Can I give my child melatonin?
q/kids-sleep-melatonin.a: Only on a paediatrician's advice. First a steady sleep routine and fewer screens.

q/kids-vitamins.a: Most children with a varied diet do not, except vitamin D for babies. Keep gummies out of reach: iron overdose is dangerous.

q/lactose-test.n: How do I know if I'm lactose intolerant?
q/lactose-test.a: Bloating or diarrhoea after milk that improves when you avoid it. There is a breath test.

q/lemon-water.n: Is lemon water in the morning good for you?
q/lemon-water.a: It is a healthy drink, but it does not "cleanse" or make you lose weight. Rinse your mouth to protect your teeth.

q/libido-supp.a: Maca and ginseng have small studies. Avoid products from the internet, which often contain hidden drugs.

q/long-covid-help.a: Pacing your energy and a gradual return to activity with medical follow-up. Supplements have no proven benefit.

q/longevity-best.n: What really makes a difference to longevity?
q/longevity-best.a: Not smoking, fitness, strength, a Mediterranean diet, sleep, social ties and blood pressure control. No supplement has been proven to extend life.

q/meat-cancer.a: Processed meats are proven carcinogens. Red meat probably is, in large amounts. Limit it to 2–3 times a week.

q/meditation-work.a: Moderate improvement in anxiety, depression and pain. Consistency matters more than duration.

q/meds-tell.n: Should I tell my doctor about supplements?
q/meds-tell.a: Yes, always, and before surgery. Many interact with medicines.

q/melatonin-dose.n: How much melatonin should I take?
q/melatonin-dose.a: Start with 0.5–1 mg, 1–2 hours before bed. Larger doses often cause a heavy head in the morning without extra benefit.

q/melatonin-safe.n: Is melatonin safe for daily use?
q/melatonin-safe.a: It does not cause dependence like sleeping pills, but long-term safety has not been well studied. Small doses (0.5–1 mg) are often enough. For chronic insomnia, CBT-I comes first.

q/memory-improve.n: How do I improve my memory?
q/memory-improve.a: Sleep, exercise, social and mental activity, checking hearing and blood pressure. Rule out B12 deficiency.

q/menopause-hrt.n: Is hormone therapy safe in menopause?
q/menopause-hrt.a: For most healthy women under 60 or within 10 years of menopause, the benefits usually outweigh the risks. The decision is individual.

q/menopause-natural.n: Are there natural remedies for hot flushes?
q/menopause-natural.a: Phytoestrogens have a small benefit and black cohosh probably none. Cognitive behavioural therapy and non-hormonal medicines are alternatives.

q/metabolism-age.a: A large study (Science 2021) showed it stays stable from 20 to 60. Muscle loss and moving less matter more.

q/metformin-b12.n: Why check B12 if I take metformin?
q/metformin-b12.a: Long-term metformin reduces B12 absorption and can cause neuropathy. Test once a year.

q/mg-diarrhea.n: Why does magnesium give me diarrhoea?
q/mg-diarrhea.a: Oxide and citrate draw water into the gut. Try glycinate or a smaller, split dose.

q/mg-forms.n: Which form of magnesium is best?
q/mg-forms.a: Glycinate is gentle on the gut and preferred for sleep. Citrate is well absorbed and helps constipation. Oxide is poorly absorbed and acts mainly as a laxative.

q/mg-when.a: Many people take it in the evening for sleep. Keep it 2 hours apart from some antibiotics and 4 hours from thyroxine.

q/mg-zn.n: Can I take magnesium and zinc together?
q/mg-zn.a: Yes, at usual doses. Very high doses of zinc (over 40 mg) lower copper.

q/migraine-supp.a: Magnesium, riboflavin (B2) 400 mg and possibly Q10 for prevention, with results after 2–3 months.

q/morning-exercise.n: Is exercise better in the morning or evening?
q/morning-exercise.a: The best time is the one you can stick to. Hard exercise very close to bedtime makes sleep harder for some people.

q/mthfr.n: I have an MTHFR mutation. Do I need methylfolate?
q/mthfr.a: The variant is very common and most people respond normally to folic acid. Methylfolate is an alternative, not a necessity.

q/multi-need.a: If you eat a varied diet, usually not. Useful with a restricted diet, older age or after bariatric surgery. It did not prevent heart disease in large studies.

q/muscle-age.a: Yes. Weight training increases strength and muscle at any age, together with enough protein.

q/nails-brittle.a: Often from water and detergents. Check iron and thyroid. Biotin only helps with a deficiency.

q/nap-ok.a: A 10–20 minute nap before 3 pm helps. Longer naps disrupt night-time sleep.

q/natural-safe.n: If it's natural, is it safe?
q/natural-safe.a: Not necessarily. Kava, black cohosh and green tea extract have caused liver damage, and St John's wort interacts with many medicines.

q/nature-health.n: Is time in nature good for you?
q/nature-health.a: 120 minutes a week is linked with better wellbeing.

q/nootropics.a: Caffeine with theanine has a small proven effect. Most others have very little data.

q/nuts-fat.a: A handful a day is not linked with weight gain in studies, despite the calories.

q/olive-oil-cook.n: Can I cook with olive oil?
q/olive-oil-cook.a: Yes. Virgin olive oil is stable at home cooking temperatures.

q/omega-fishburp.n: Omega-3 gives me fishy burps. What do I do?
q/omega-fishburp.a: Take them with food, try frozen or enteric-coated capsules, or the triglyceride form.

q/omega-how.n: How much omega-3 do I need?
q/omega-how.a: For general health 250–500 mg EPA+DHA, which 2 portions of oily fish a week provide. Higher doses (2–4 g) for triglycerides, with a doctor.

q/omega-label.n: How do I read an omega-3 label?
q/omega-label.a: What matters is EPA+DHA per dose, not the capsule weight. A 1000 mg capsule may contain only 300 mg EPA+DHA.

q/organic.a: It has fewer pesticide residues, but no meaningful health difference has been proven. Eating more fruit and vegetables matters more.

q/osteo-calcium.n: Do I need calcium for my bones?
q/osteo-calcium.a: Get it from food first (dairy, sardines, tahini). A supplement if your diet falls short, up to 500 mg per dose.

q/osteo-exercise.n: Which exercise is good for the bones?
q/osteo-exercise.a: Weight-bearing and impact exercise (walking, stair climbing, gentle jumps if allowed). Swimming does not load the bones enough.

q/palpitations-coffee.n: Is coffee to blame for palpitations?
q/palpitations-coffee.a: Sometimes, especially at high doses and with energy drinks. Palpitations with chest pain or fainting need urgent assessment.

q/pcos-inositol.a: Studies show improvement in cycles and insulin. Weight loss and exercise remain the foundation.

q/period-pain.a: A hot water bottle, anti-inflammatory painkillers and gentle exercise. Ginger has small positive studies. Pain that gets worse needs checking for endometriosis.

q/pms-help.a: Exercise, calcium, vitamin B6 (up to 100 mg) and chasteberry (vitex). With severe mental symptoms, see a doctor.

q/posture-pain.n: Is bad posture to blame for neck pain?
q/posture-pain.a: The link is weaker than people think. Movement breaks and strengthening help more.

q/ppi-mg.a: Long-term use lowers B12, magnesium, calcium and iron. Discuss whether you still need the medicine.

q/pregnancy-safe.n: Which supplements are safe in pregnancy?
q/pregnancy-safe.a: Folic acid, iodine, vitamin D and iron if needed. Most herbs have no safety data. Avoid high-dose vitamin A.

q/preworkout.a: They often contain very high caffeine and sometimes banned stimulants. Take care if you have arrhythmias or high blood pressure.

q/probiotic-antibiotic.n: Should I take a probiotic with antibiotics?
q/probiotic-antibiotic.a: It reduces diarrhoea from antibiotics. S. boulardii can be taken at the same time, bacterial strains 2 hours after.

q/probiotic-choose.n: How do I choose a probiotic?
q/probiotic-choose.a: Choose a strain studied for your problem: e.g. S. boulardii or LGG with antibiotics. Billions of CFU alone say little.

q/prostate-supp.a: Saw palmetto showed no benefit in large studies. Urinary symptoms need a urologist.

q/protein-kidney.n: Does a lot of protein harm the kidneys?
q/protein-kidney.a: No harm has been found in healthy kidneys. With chronic kidney disease the nephrologist sets the limit.

q/protein-needed.a: Not if you get enough protein from food. It is simply a practical source.

q/protein-timing.n: Must I take protein right after training?
q/protein-timing.a: The total daily amount matters more than the exact time. Spreading it over 3–4 meals is good practice.

q/psoriasis-diet.a: Weight loss in people who are overweight improves the disease. Supplements have little benefit.

q/quality.n: How do I know a supplement is good quality?
q/quality.a: Look for independent certification (USP, NSF, Informed Sport), the exact form and dose on the label, and avoid "proprietary blends" and exaggerated promises. Check that it is registered with your national regulator.

q/quit-smoking-how.n: What is the best way to quit smoking?
q/quit-smoking-how.a: Combining counselling with medication (nicotine replacement, varenicline) gives the best chances. Public stop-smoking services are often free.

q/quit-smoking-weight.n: Will I gain weight if I quit smoking?
q/quit-smoking-weight.a: Often 3–5 kilos, but the health benefit is far greater. Exercise and fruit snacks help.

q/reflux-help.a: Smaller meals, no food for 3 hours before bed, raising the head of the bed, weight loss. Peppermint makes it worse.

q/running-knees.a: In recreational runners it does not increase osteoarthritis. Increasing gradually prevents injuries.

q/salt-howmuch.a: Less than 5 g a day (one teaspoon), including the "hidden" salt in bread, cheese and ready meals.

q/sauna-work.n: Is the sauna good for you?
q/sauna-work.a: Observational data from Finland show fewer cardiovascular events. Drink water and no alcohol.

q/screens-sleep.n: Does my phone affect my sleep?
q/screens-sleep.a: Yes, the light and activity delay sleep. Turn screens off 30–60 minutes before bed.

q/selenium-hashimoto.a: It lowers antibodies, but it has not been shown to change the course or replace thyroxine.

q/shift-sleep.n: How do I sleep after a night shift?
q/shift-sleep.a: Sunglasses on the way home, a dark and cool room, caffeine only at the start of the shift.

q/sitting-risk.n: Is sitting a lot really that bad?
q/sitting-risk.a: Yes, but 60–75 minutes of moderate activity a day offsets the risk.

q/skin-glow.a: Sunscreen, quitting smoking, sleep and moisturising. Topical retinoids have the best evidence against ageing.

q/sleep-best.a: None is as effective as changing habits: a fixed schedule, morning light, less caffeine and alcohol. Melatonin helps with jet lag and falling asleep.

q/sleep-hours.n: How many hours of sleep do I need?
q/sleep-hours.a: Most adults need 7–9. A steady schedule is just as important.

q/snoring-help.n: What can I do about snoring?
q/snoring-help.a: Weight loss, sleeping on your side, no alcohol in the evening. With pauses in breathing, a sleep study.

q/social-health.a: Yes. Strong social ties are linked with about 50% greater survival.

q/soy-safe.a: Yes, in normal amounts, even for women with a history of breast cancer and for men.

q/sparkling-ok.n: Is sparkling water bad for you?
q/sparkling-ok.a: No, it is safe for most people. It may cause bloating in some.

q/spinach-iron.n: Does spinach have a lot of iron?
q/spinach-iron.a: It has iron but little is absorbed because of oxalates. Lemon helps a little.

q/statin-coq10.n: Do I need Q10 if I take a statin?
q/statin-coq10.a: Statins lower Q10, but studies on muscle pain are conflicting. First discuss a change of dose or medicine with your doctor.

q/steps-howmany.n: How many steps a day do I need?
q/steps-howmany.a: The mortality benefit levels off at about 6,000–8,000 steps after 60 and 8,000–10,000 in younger people. Every extra step counts.

q/stjohns-why.n: Why is St John's wort dangerous?
q/stjohns-why.a: It reduces the effect of many medicines (contraceptives, anticoagulants, antiretrovirals) and with antidepressants it causes serotonin syndrome.

q/stress-quick.a: Slow breathing with a long exhale for 5 minutes, a short walk and less caffeine. For chronic anxiety, psychotherapy.

q/stretch-before.a: A dynamic warm-up before and stretching after is better.

q/sugar-craving.n: How do I stop sugar cravings?
q/sugar-craving.a: Protein and fibre with every meal, enough sleep and cutting down gradually. Cravings usually fade after 2–3 weeks.

q/sugar-food.a: Weight loss, walking after meals, weight training, fewer sugary drinks and more fibre.

q/sunlight-d.n: How much sun do I need for vitamin D?
q/sunlight-d.a: In summer 10–20 minutes on arms and legs, without burning. In winter, production is low at mid and northern latitudes.

q/sunscreen-d.a: Very little in real-life conditions. Don't stop using sunscreen for the sake of vitamin D.

q/supp-overdose.a: Yes, mainly on the fat-soluble ones (A, D) and iron. B6 at high doses for months causes neuropathy. Stick to the upper limits.

q/surgery-stop.n: Which supplements should I stop before surgery?
q/surgery-stop.a: Usually 1–2 weeks before: ginkgo, garlic capsules, high-dose omega-3, vitamin E, St John's wort, kava, valerian, ginseng. Follow your anaesthetist's advice.

q/sweeteners-ok.a: They are approved in sensible amounts. The WHO does not recommend them for weight loss, and aspartame was classed as "possibly carcinogenic" on very limited evidence.

q/testosterone-natural.n: How do I raise testosterone naturally?
q/testosterone-natural.a: Weight loss, 7–9 hours of sleep and weight training. Testosterone "boosters" usually do not work.

q/thal-iron.n: I carry the thalassaemia trait. Can I take iron?
q/thal-iron.a: Only if tests also show iron deficiency (low ferritin) and your doctor approves. The trait alone does not need iron.

q/thyroid-biotin.n: Why stop biotin before thyroid tests?
q/thyroid-biotin.a: Biotin distorts many tests and can falsely suggest hyperthyroidism. Stop it 2–3 days before.

q/thyroid-coffee.n: How long after thyroxine can I drink coffee?
q/thyroid-coffee.a: At least 30–60 minutes. Calcium, iron and magnesium at least 4 hours after.

q/thyroid-iodine.n: Do I need iodine for my thyroid?
q/thyroid-iodine.a: Iodised salt is usually enough. With Hashimoto's or hyperthyroidism, seaweed and high doses of iodine may cause harm.

q/together.n: Which supplements should I not take together?
q/together.a: Calcium with iron (they compete), high-dose zinc with copper, and calcium, iron and magnesium close to thyroxine or some antibiotics.

q/urine-yellow.n: Why did vitamins turn my urine yellow?
q/urine-yellow.a: From the riboflavin (B2) in B complexes. It is harmless.

q/uti-cranberry.a: It helps prevent them in women with recurrences, not treat an active infection.

q/vaccines-adults.a: Flu every year, tetanus every 10 years, pneumococcus and shingles depending on age, and others as your doctor recommends.

q/vaping-safer.a: It is less harmful than smoking but not harmless, and it keeps the addiction going. As a quitting aid it has some evidence.

q/varicose-help.a: Compression stockings, walking, raising the legs. Horse chestnut has some evidence for the symptoms.

q/vegan-complete.n: Can a vegan diet be complete?
q/vegan-complete.a: Yes, with careful planning and B12. Pay attention to iodine, omega-3, vitamin D, calcium, iron and zinc.

q/warfarin-greens.n: Can I eat green vegetables on warfarin?
q/warfarin-greens.a: Yes, but in a steady amount each week so your INR does not change.

q/water-howmuch.n: How much water should I drink?
q/water-howmuch.a: Enough not to feel thirsty and to have pale urine. Needs rise in heat and with exercise. There is no magic number.

q/weight-drugs.n: What are the new weight loss medicines?
q/weight-drugs.a: Medicines such as semaglutide and tirzepatide cause significant weight loss. They are given on prescription with medical follow-up.

q/weight-loss-best.n: Which diet is best for weight loss?
q/weight-loss-best.a: The one you can stick to. Studies show similar results for low-fat and low-carb diets when calories are the same.

q/weight-plateau.n: Why did I stop losing weight?
q/weight-plateau.a: At a lower weight you need fewer calories, and intake often creeps back up without you noticing. Food tracking and weight training help.

q/wine-heart.n: Is a glass of wine good for the heart?
q/wine-heart.a: Newer studies do not confirm a benefit. Alcohol raises cancer risk even in small amounts.

q/yoga-back.n: Does yoga help low back pain?
q/yoga-back.a: Yes, for chronic low back pain, with moderate evidence.

q/yogurt-probiotic.a: It contains live cultures, but not always the strains studied for specific problems. It is a good everyday choice.

q/zn-cold.a: Zinc lozenges within the first 24 hours may shorten the cold. Long-term high doses lower copper.

why_v: Nicotinamide for skin cancer in high-risk people
why_u: One of the most common reports of improvement

s/adhd.alert: Diagnosis and treatment are done by a child psychiatrist or psychiatrist.

s/afib.alert: Often needs an anticoagulant. Many supplements interact with it.
avoid: Raise the risk of atrial fibrillation
Vitamin K, ginkgo, turmeric with anticoagulants
why_v: With low magnesium, with a doctor

s/alcoholuse.alert: Stopping suddenly after heavy use can cause seizures: medical help is needed.

s/alopecia_areata.alert: Autoimmune. Newer medicines are available from a dermatologist.

s/alzheimers.alert: Sudden confusion may be an infection or a medicine. Diagnosis is made by a neurologist.
why_v: If there is a deficiency, which can look like dementia
B6/B9/B12 slowed brain shrinkage with high homocysteine (VITACOG)

s/anemia.alert: Anaemia has many causes and treatment depends on the cause. Before any supplement you need tests: full blood count, ferritin, B12, folate and, if the red cells are small, haemoglobin electrophoresis. Iron only helps in iron-deficiency anaemia.
avoid: In thalassaemia and haemochromatosis iron builds up and damages the heart, liver and endocrine glands.
diff: Inherited. Small red cells as in iron deficiency, but usually with normal or high ferritin
Haemolysis after broad beans or certain medicines
why_v: Only in megaloblastic anaemia from B12 deficiency
why_u: With iron for absorption, only in iron deficiency

s/ankylosing.alert: Inflammatory back pain that improves with movement. Needs a rheumatologist.

s/anosmia.alert: Sudden loss without a cold needs examination.

s/anticoag.alert: Many supplements raise bleeding risk or change how the medicine works. Tell your doctor about every supplement.
avoid: Vitamin K1/K2 with warfarin without a steady dose
Ginkgo, turmeric, high-dose omega-3, garlic capsules

s/aphthae.alert: An ulcer that does not heal in 3 weeks needs examination.

s/appetite_loss.alert: Long-lasting loss of appetite with weight loss needs a medical check.

s/asthma.alert: Inhaled treatment is the foundation. Difficulty speaking or blue lips need emergency services immediately.
avoid: Aspirin in people for whom it is contraindicated
why_v: Fewer severe attacks in people with deficiency

s/b12def.alert: Causes: vegan diet, metformin, antacids, gastritis, pernicious anaemia. Pernicious anaemia often needs injections.
avoid: May hide the deficiency while nerve damage progresses
why_v: High dose by mouth or injections depending on the cause

s/backpain.alert: Pain with fever, loss of bladder or bowel control, weakness in the legs or after a fall needs a doctor immediately.

s/bariatric.alert: Lifelong supplements and regular tests are needed.

s/bipolar.alert: Needs a psychiatrist. Some supplements can trigger mania.
avoid: Lithium as a supplement without a psychiatrist
why_v: As an add-on, small benefit in depression

s/bloating.alert: Persistent bloating with weight loss or after 50 needs checking.

why_v: Together with D in older adults

s/bph.alert: Symptoms need a urology check and a PSA test at the doctor's discretion.

s/brainfog.alert: Check sleep, thyroid, B12, iron, depression and medicines.

s/breastfeeding.alert: Many herbs and supplements pass into breast milk.
avoid: Large doses of herbs for "more milk"

s/bv.alert: Itching with discharge is not always thrush. With recurrences, see a gynaecologist.
avoid: Essential oil preparations inside the vagina

s/cad.n: Coronary heart disease / after a heart attack
s/cad.alert: Chest pain lasting more than 5 minutes: call emergency services. Supplements do not replace statins and aspirin.
avoid: Red yeast rice together with a statin
why_v: With high triglycerides, with a cardiologist

s/carpaltunnel.alert: Weakness in the hand needs an orthopaedic surgeon or neurologist.
why_v: Old studies, take care with the dose

s/cataract.alert: Treatment is surgical and very effective.

s/celiac.alert: Do not start a gluten-free diet before testing: results come back falsely negative.

s/cellulite.alert: A cosmetic issue, not a disease. Not to be confused with cellulitis, a skin infection.

s/cfs.alert: Worsening after exertion is typical: a sudden increase in exercise can cause harm.
diff: Ordinary tiredness with a recognisable cause

s/chemo.alert: Tell your oncologist about every supplement. Some antioxidants and herbs may reduce how well treatment works.
avoid: Lowers levels of many chemotherapy drugs

s/cirrhosis.alert: Many supplements and herbs strain the liver or build up. Every product needs a hepatologist's approval.
lifex: Late-evening snack with carbohydrate and protein
why_v: Enough protein (ESPEN guidelines), with a doctor

s/ckd.alert: In kidney disease many supplements build up in the body. Every supplement, including "natural" ones, needs your nephrologist's approval.
avoid: Distorts creatinine measurement and adds strain.
Some strain the kidneys or interact with medicines.
why_v: Only the form and dose set by your nephrologist
s: International guidelines for chronic kidney disease, including avoiding medicines and substances that strain the kidneys.
KDIGO 2024 clinical practice guideline for the evaluation and management of chronic kidney disease

s/coldhands.alert: May be due to anaemia, hypothyroidism or Raynaud's.

s/colic.alert: Fever, vomiting, refusing feeds or weight loss in a baby need a paediatrician immediately.

s/constipation.alert: A sudden change after 50, blood or weight loss need checking.
avoid: Frequent use of stimulant laxatives (senna, aloe)

s/copd.alert: Quitting smoking is the only intervention that changes the course of the disease.

s/cough.alert: A cough lasting more than 3 weeks, with blood, breathlessness or high fever needs a doctor.

s/covid.alert: Breathlessness, chest pain or oxygen saturation below 94% need a doctor immediately. High-risk groups should ask early about antivirals.
why_v: With deficiency, no clear benefit as treatment

s/cramps_exercise.alert: Usually due to muscle fatigue more than electrolytes.
why_v: In long exercise in the heat

s/cramps_period.alert: Pain that increases over the years or does not ease needs a gynaecologist to check for endometriosis.
lifex: Hot water bottle on the belly

s/depression.alert: If you have thoughts of self-harm, seek help immediately: call your local crisis line or emergency services. Supplements do not replace treatment.
avoid: St John's wort, 5-HTP, SAMe together with antidepressants
why_v: As an add-on with a psychiatrist

s/diarrhea.alert: Blood, high fever, signs of dehydration or lasting more than 3 days need a doctor. Babies and older people dehydrate quickly.
avoid: Sports drinks and soft drinks for rehydration
lifex: Keep eating when you have an appetite

s/diverticular.alert: Pain in the lower left belly with fever may be diverticulitis and needs a doctor.

s/doms.alert: Very severe pain with dark urine after exercise may be rhabdomyolysis: see a doctor immediately.

s/drymouth.alert: Often caused by medicines. It may also be Sjögren's syndrome.

s/eatingdisorder.alert: A serious but treatable condition. Seek help from a doctor or mental health professional.

s/eczema.alert: The foundation of treatment is moisturising the skin every day.
why_v: Small benefit for prevention in babies

s/ed.alert: Often the first sign of cardiovascular disease or diabetes. Needs a medical check.

s/edema.alert: Swelling with breathlessness may be heart failure. Swelling in one calf: check for a blood clot.

s/elderly.alert: With age, B12 absorption and the skin's vitamin D production fall, while protein needs rise.
avoid: Many supplements together with many medicines

s/endometriosis.alert: Severe period pain that does not ease with painkillers needs a gynaecologist.

s/epilepsy.alert: Some herbs and supplements interact with anti-seizure medicines or lower the seizure threshold.
why_v: Essential before pregnancy on anti-seizure medicines

s/eyes_dry.alert: Pain, redness with blurred vision or light sensitivity need an eye doctor.
why_v: The large DREAM trial showed no benefit

s/eyestrain.alert: Headache with blurred vision may mean you need glasses.

s/falls.alert: Reviewing medicines, eyesight and the home reduces falls.
avoid: Very large one-off doses of vitamin D
why_v: With deficiency, not large one-off doses

s/fibromyalgia.alert: Needs diagnosis by a rheumatologist to rule out other causes.

s/flu.alert: High-risk groups need a doctor early for antivirals. Vaccination is the best prevention.

s/foodallergy.alert: Swelling of the lips or throat, difficulty breathing or dizziness is an emergency: call emergency services and use adrenaline if you have it.

s/g6pd.alert: In G6PD deficiency certain substances destroy red blood cells (haemolysis). Ask your doctor or pharmacist before any supplement or herb.
avoid: The main cause of haemolysis in favism.
Very high doses of vitamin C (especially intravenous)
Haemolysis has been reported. Normal dietary amounts are safe.
E.g. some antimalarials, sulfonamides, naphthalene, methylene blue. There is an official list
diff: A different inherited condition, but they can occur together
why_v: In chronic haemolysis, only on medical advice
s: G6PD deficiency: haemolysis from broad beans, medicines and infections, and how to prevent it.
Cappellini Fiorelli 2008 glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency Lancet
Classification of G6PD deficiency and substances that cause haemolysis.
WHO Working Group 1989 glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency

s/gad.alert: Psychotherapy (cognitive behavioural) and medicines have the strongest evidence.
diff: Everyday stress is not a disorder

s/gallstones.alert: Pain in the upper right belly with fever or jaundice needs a doctor immediately.

s/gastritis.alert: Helicobacter is treated with antibiotics. Pain with black stools or vomiting blood needs a doctor immediately.
avoid: Anti-inflammatories and aspirin without stomach protection
why_v: Fewer side effects of eradication therapy

s/gerd.alert: Difficulty swallowing, weight loss, vomiting blood or black stools need a doctor immediately. Long-term antacid use lowers B12 and magnesium.
lifex: Raising the head of the bed
Less alcohol, coffee, fatty food if they make it worse
why_v: If you have taken proton pump inhibitors for years

s/gestdiab.alert: Needs follow-up by an obstetrician and dietitian.

s/glaucoma.alert: Needs regular follow-up and eye drops. Untreated it causes blindness.

s/gout.alert: Attacks need treatment. If uric acid is high, the doctor may suggest long-term treatment.
avoid: Soft drinks and juices with fructose

s/graves.alert: This is about an overactive thyroid. Advice for Hashimoto's does not apply here.
avoid: "Thyroid support" supplements containing hormones or iodine
Often do not list their contents correctly.
why_v: In mild Graves' eye disease, 100 µg twice a day for 6 months, on an endocrinologist's advice
Bones are affected. Measure and replace if needed
s: Selenium improved quality of life and slowed mild Graves' eye disease.
Marcocci 2011 selenium and the course of mild Graves orbitopathy

s/growing_pains.alert: Pain on one side, fever, swelling or limping need a paediatrician.

s/gum.alert: Needs a professional clean by a dentist.
lifex: Brushing twice a day and flossing

s/hairgrey.alert: Usually hereditary. Less often linked with B12 or the thyroid.

s/hangover.alert: No supplement has been proven. The only prevention is less alcohol.
avoid: Paracetamol after a lot of alcohol

s/heavyperiods.alert: The most common cause of iron deficiency in women. Needs a gynaecological check.
avoid: Ginkgo, high-dose omega-3 and other "blood thinners"

s/hemochromatosis.alert: The body absorbs and stores too much iron. Treatment is blood removal (venesection) with medical follow-up.
avoid: Risk of serious Vibrio vulnificus infection with iron overload.
Adds strain to an already stressed liver.
diff: The opposite problem: deficiency instead of excess
s: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL)
Guidelines for haemochromatosis: venesection, avoiding iron and vitamin C supplements.
EASL clinical practice guidelines on haemochromatosis 2022

s/hemorrhoids.alert: Blood in the stool over the age of 45–50 needs checking to rule out other causes.

s/hepatitis.alert: Effective antivirals exist. Hepatitis C can now be fully cured.
avoid: Herbs with liver toxicity (kava, black cohosh, green tea capsules)
lifex: Hepatitis A and B vaccines if needed

s/herpes.alert: Antiviral creams or tablets at the first signs shorten the outbreak.

s/highldl.alert: At high risk, statins have strong proof of reducing heart attacks.
avoid: Red yeast rice together with a statin

s/hightg.alert: Levels above 500 mg/dl raise the risk of pancreatitis.

s/hiv.alert: With proper antiretroviral treatment, life expectancy is near normal. Many herbs affect the medicines.

s/ibd.alert: Needs a gastroenterologist. Deficiencies of iron, B12, D and zinc are common.

s/immunelow.alert: Very frequent or severe infections need a medical check.

s/infertility_f.alert: After 12 months of trying (6 after 35) both partners need testing.
avoid: Herbs and hormones without a doctor

s/infertility_m.alert: Investigation is done by a urologist-andrologist.
why_v: Large trial (FAZST) showed no fertility benefit

why_u: Glycinate is one of the most mentioned for sleep

s/irondef.alert: The cause must be found: heavy periods, blood loss from the gut, coeliac disease, diet.
diff: Small red cells with normal ferritin

why_u: A small dose at the right time

s/kidneystones.alert: The type of stone (e.g. calcium oxalate, uric acid) determines the advice.
lifex: Enough water to pass more than 2–2.5 litres of urine a day

s/kids_adhd_diet.alert: Sugar does not cause hyperactivity in studies. Some artificial colourings slightly affect some children.

s/kids_picky.alert: Slow growth or weight loss needs a paediatrician.
avoid: Risk of overdose, they look like sweets
why_v: Children's formula, if the diet is very limited

s/knee_oa.alert: Exercise and weight loss have the strongest evidence.
lifex: Every kilo reduces the load on the knee

s/lactoseint.alert: It is not an allergy. Milk allergy is a different, more serious condition.
lifex: Small amounts of milk with food

s/longcovid.alert: Symptoms more than 3 months after infection need a medical assessment.

s/lowbp.alert: Fainting or dizziness with falls needs a review of medicines and the heart.
lifex: Water and enough salt if your doctor allows

s/lowlibido.alert: Often linked with medicines (antidepressants), fatigue or the relationship.

s/lowt.alert: Diagnosis needs two morning measurements and symptoms.

s/lupus.alert: An autoimmune disease. Needs a rheumatologist.
why_v: With deficiency, common because of sun avoidance

s/mci.alert: Needs checking for reversible causes (B12, thyroid, depression, medicines, sleep).
lifex: Hearing aids if hearing is impaired

s/meds_diuretics.alert: Diuretics change potassium, magnesium and sodium. Regular blood tests are essential.
avoid: Potassium and salt substitutes with potassium-sparing diuretics

s/meds_levo.alert: Thyroxine is taken on an empty stomach. Many supplements reduce its absorption.
avoid: Psyllium and fibre at the same time

s/meds_metformin.alert: Long-term metformin lowers B12. Yearly testing is recommended.

s/meds_ocp.alert: Some herbs reduce how well the pill works.
avoid: Activated charcoal close to the pill
why_v: If you are planning a pregnancy

s/meds_ppi.alert: Long-term use lowers B12, magnesium, calcium and iron. Whether you still need it should be reviewed.

s/meds_ssri.alert: Some supplements combined with them cause serotonin syndrome (agitation, fever, tremor, fast heart rate).

s/meds_statin.alert: Do not stop your statin without your doctor. Muscle pain often resolves with a change of dose or medicine.

s/meds_steroids.alert: Long-term steroids cause osteoporosis. Your doctor may also suggest a bone medicine.

s/menopause.alert: Hormone therapy is the most effective treatment for hot flushes and safe for many women: discuss it with your gynaecologist.
avoid: Phytoestrogens with a history of breast cancer
lifex: Cognitive behavioural therapy for hot flushes
why_v: No benefit in Cochrane, liver toxicity
For the bones if the diet falls short

s/metsyn.alert: A combination of belly fat, high blood pressure, blood sugar and lipids. Greatly raises cardiovascular risk.

s/morningsickness.alert: Severe vomiting that stops you keeping fluids down (hyperemesis) needs a doctor immediately.

s/motionsick.alert: Pharmacy antihistamines help but cause drowsiness.
lifex: Look at the horizon, sit in the front

s/ms.alert: Disease-modifying treatment from a neurologist is the foundation.
why_v: Low levels are linked with disease activity

why_u: The most common recommendation in fitness forums

s/nafld.alert: Many liver "detox" products do not help and some cause harm. Weight loss is the most effective treatment.
diff: A different cause of liver strain
why_v: 800 IU in steatohepatitis without diabetes, only with a hepatologist

s/nails_fungus.alert: Needs confirmation. Tablets from a dermatologist work better than nail lacquers.
avoid: Essential oils as the only treatment

s/nausea.alert: Nausea with severe pain, fever, headache or in pregnancy needs a doctor.

s/neckpain.alert: Pain with numbness or weakness in the arms needs examination.

s/nightmares.alert: Some supplements (B6, melatonin) cause vivid dreams. Recurring nightmares after trauma need a specialist.
avoid: B6 and melatonin in the evening

why_u: Went away after correcting the deficiency

s/obesity.alert: Effective medicines now exist. Talk to your doctor, especially if you also have diabetes or high blood pressure.

s/ocd.alert: Treated with psychotherapy (exposure and response prevention) and medicines.
avoid: Combinations with antidepressants without a doctor

s/oral_health_halitosis.alert: Usually comes from the tongue and gums. May be linked with tonsils or sinusitis.

s/osteoarthritis_hand.alert: Swollen, warm joints with morning stiffness over an hour may be inflammatory arthritis.

s/osteopenia.alert: A stage before osteoporosis. The doctor estimates fracture risk (FRAX).

s/osteoporosis_men.alert: There is often a secondary cause (steroids, alcohol, low testosterone).

s/overtraining.alert: A long-lasting drop in performance with fatigue and poor sleep needs rest and a check-up.

s/pad.alert: Calf pain when walking that goes away with rest. A sign of widespread atherosclerosis.

s/palpitations.alert: Palpitations with chest pain, fainting or breathlessness: call emergency services.

s/pancreatitis.alert: Needs a gastroenterologist. Prescription enzymes are often needed.

s/panic.alert: A first attack with chest pain needs checking to rule out a heart cause. Psychotherapy is very effective.

s/parkinsons.alert: Levodopa is affected by protein and iron: ask your neurologist about timing.
avoid: Iron at the same time as levodopa
High-dose B6 with levodopa without carbidopa
why_v: With deficiency, for bones and falls

s/pcos.alert: Needs a gynaecologist or endocrinologist. Affects cycles, fertility, blood sugar and skin.

s/perimenopause.alert: Irregular cycles, sleep and mood change. Contraception is needed until 12 months without a period.

s/plantar.alert: Usually settles within months with stretching and suitable shoes.

s/pmdd.alert: A more severe form of premenstrual syndrome with strong mental symptoms. Effective treatment exists.

s/postpartum.alert: If your mood has been low for more than 2 weeks or you have thoughts of harm, seek help immediately (local crisis line or emergency services). It is common and treatable.
lifex: Sleep with help from your partner or family

s/prediabetes.alert: Lifestyle change reduces diabetes risk by about 58% (Diabetes Prevention Program), more than medicines.
diff: The next stage if nothing changes
lifex: Losing 7% of body weight and 150 minutes of exercise a week

s/preeclampsia.alert: Urgent. Headache, blurred vision, pain under the ribs or a swollen face in pregnancy: go to the maternity unit immediately.
lifex: Low-dose aspirin only if your obstetrician recommends it
why_v: With low calcium intake, WHO recommendation

s/pregplan.alert: Folic acid must be started before conception.

s/psoriasis.alert: A chronic autoimmune condition. Linked with cardiovascular risk and arthritis.
avoid: High-dose vitamin A without a dermatologist
lifex: Improves the disease in people who are overweight
why_v: By mouth, mixed results. Topical analogues are a treatment

s/ra.alert: An autoimmune disease. Early treatment by a rheumatologist prevents permanent damage.
why_v: Small reduction in pain and need for anti-inflammatories

s/raynaud.alert: If it starts after 30 or with pain and sores on the fingers, it needs a rheumatology check.

s/red_s.alert: Missing periods in an athlete is not normal and affects the bones.

s/rhinitis.alert: Antihistamines and steroid nasal sprays are effective and safe.
avoid: Echinacea in people allergic to daisies
diff: Infectious, with fever or sore throat

s/rls.alert: Measure ferritin: guidelines suggest iron if it is below 75 ng/ml.
avoid: Caffeine and alcohol in the evening

lifex: Avoiding alcohol, spicy food and very hot drinks if they trigger it
why_v: The dry eye of the condition

s/sarcopenia.alert: Resistance exercise is the main treatment.

s/seasonal.alert: Light therapy with a special lamp has good evidence.
lifex: Morning daylight or a 10,000 lux light therapy lamp
Shampoo with ketoconazole or zinc pyrithione

s/shiftwork.alert: Drowsy driving after a night shift is dangerous.
avoid: Caffeine at the end of the shift
lifex: A dark room, sunglasses on the way home
A short nap before the shift
why_v: At the start of the shift

s/shingles.alert: Antivirals within 72 hours. On the face or near the eye, see a doctor immediately. A vaccine is available for people over 50.

s/sibo.alert: Diagnosis and treatment (usually an antibiotic) are done by a gastroenterologist.

s/sicklecell.alert: An inherited condition that needs a haematologist. Iron is not given without checking ferritin.
diff: A related condition, they often occur together

s/sinusitis.alert: Most episodes are viral and pass in 7–10 days. Swelling around the eye or a severe headache needs a doctor.

s/sjogren.alert: An autoimmune disease with dry mouth and eyes. Needs a rheumatologist.

s/sleepapnea.alert: Loud snoring with pauses in breathing and daytime sleepiness needs a sleep study. It raises the risk of accidents and heart disease.
avoid: Sleeping pills, sedatives and alcohol in the evening
diff: Difficulty sleeping, not pauses in breathing

s/smoker.alert: Quitting is the most beneficial step. Some supplements harm smokers.
why_v: Smokers need 35 mg more a day

s/snoring.alert: Snoring with pauses in breathing and daytime sleepiness: get checked for sleep apnoea.

s/sore_throat.alert: Difficulty swallowing or breathing, drooling or high fever need a doctor.
lifex: Honey in warm water (not for babies)

s/stress_burnout.alert: If it comes with low mood or insomnia for weeks, talk to a doctor.

s/stressfracture.alert: Common in athletes with inadequate nutrition or disrupted cycles.

s/stroke.alert: Sudden weakness, a drooping mouth or difficulty speaking: call emergency services immediately.

s/sunburn.alert: Some medicines and herbs (e.g. St John's wort) increase sensitivity to the sun.
why_v: Nicotinamide for fewer skin cancers at high risk

s/surgery.alert: Tell your anaesthetist. Many supplements are stopped 1–2 weeks before.
avoid: Ginkgo, garlic capsules, high-dose omega-3, vitamin E
lifex: Quitting smoking at least 4 weeks before

s/sweating.alert: Night sweats with fever or weight loss need a doctor.

s/t1d.alert: An autoimmune disease that always needs insulin. No supplement replaces it.
lifex: Regular exercise with blood sugar monitoring

s/t2d.alert: Supplements do not replace treatment. Some lower blood sugar and together with medicines may cause hypoglycaemia.
why_v: Check B12 if you take metformin

s/teen_acne.alert: Severe acne leaves scars: see a dermatologist early.
avoid: Makes it worse in some people
lifex: Less sugar and dairy if they make it worse

s/tendinopathy.alert: Sudden pain with a "snap" in the Achilles may be a rupture.
why_v: With vitamin C before exercise, small studies

s/tensionheadache.alert: A sudden, very severe headache, fever with a stiff neck or neurological symptoms need a doctor immediately.
avoid: Painkillers on more than 10–15 days a month

s/thalassemia.alert: Thalassaemia is inherited and differs from iron-deficiency anaemia. Do not take iron, not even in multivitamins, unless your haematologist tells you to. In severe forms, transfusions cause iron overload. In the "trait" (carrier), iron only helps if tests also show iron deficiency.
avoid: Risk of iron overload. Only if ferritin is low and your doctor approves.
Increase iron absorption. Taken only if the haematologist prescribes it, e.g. with desferrioxamine.
diff: Iron deficiency is treated with iron, thalassaemia is not
lifex: May reduce iron absorption from food (de Alarcon 1979)
why_v: Often recommended because of increased red cell production, especially in the intermediate form without transfusions. Only with the haematologist
Osteoporosis is common. Measure levels and replace if needed
For the bones, if the diet falls short
Deficiency is common with some chelation medicines. Only after testing
why_u: Many patients take it regularly on their haematologist's advice
Less bone pain is often reported once the deficiency is corrected
s: Taher AT, Weatherall DJ, Cappellini MD
Modern overview of thalassaemia: diagnosis, iron overload, chelation therapy, complications.
Cappellini MD, Farmakis D, Porter J, Taher A (TIF)
Guidelines for transfusion-dependent thalassaemia: avoiding iron, chelation, bones, vitamin D.

Tea with meals reduced iron absorption in thalassaemia.
