Bone disease is common in thalassaemia and linked with vitamin D deficiency.
Vogiatzi 2009 bone disease in thalassemia frequent and still unresolved problem

s/thyroid.alert: Only for Hashimoto's thyroiditis and hypothyroidism. Different advice applies to hyperthyroidism (Graves'). Supplements do not replace thyroxine.
avoid: Calcium, iron, magnesium close to thyroxine
Reduce its absorption. Keep at least 4 hours apart.
why_u: Some report worsening with high doses

s/thyroid_nodule.alert: Most are benign. They are assessed with an ultrasound.
avoid: Iodine and seaweed without an endocrinologist

s/tinnitus.alert: Tinnitus in one ear, sudden hearing loss or vertigo need an ENT specialist.
lifex: Sound therapy and cognitive behavioural therapy

s/travelers_diarrhea.alert: With blood or high fever, see a doctor.

s/underweight.alert: Unexplained weight loss needs a medical check.
lifex: More frequent meals with nuts, olive oil

s/uti.alert: Fever, back pain or blood in the urine need a doctor. Men and pregnant women should always see a doctor.

s/varicose.alert: Sudden pain and swelling in one calf may be a blood clot: see a doctor immediately.

s/vegan.alert: A vegan diet always needs B12.
why_v: If there are no fortified foods

s/vertigo.alert: Dizziness with weakness, double vision or difficulty speaking: call emergency services. Benign positional vertigo is treated with repositioning manoeuvres.
why_v: Fewer recurrences of benign positional vertigo with deficiency

s/vitddef.alert: 25(OH)D levels below 20 ng/ml are considered deficient. Retest after 3 months of replacement.
lifex: 10–20 minutes of sun in the warm months
why_v: With a doctor for severe deficiency

s/vitiligo.alert: Autoimmune. Treated with phototherapy and topical medicines.

s/weightgain.alert: Rapid gain with swollen legs or breathlessness needs a doctor. Check thyroid and medicines.

s/wound.alert: A wound that does not heal, especially a diabetic foot, needs a doctor.
why_v: In pressure sores, in special formulas

q/d-howmuch.n: How much vitamin D do I need?
q/d-howmuch.a: Most adults are covered by 600–800 IU a day, while correcting a deficiency usually takes 1000–2000 IU. Over 4000 IU only on medical advice. A 25(OH)D test shows what you need.

q/d-k2.n: Should I take K2 with D3?
q/d-k2.a: The combination is popular, but it has not been shown to be better than D alone. If you take warfarin, K2 changes how it works.

q/d-test.n: Do I need to test my vitamin D?
q/d-test.a: Yes, if you are at risk of deficiency (little sun, obesity, osteoporosis, malabsorption, dark skin). For the general population, guidelines do not recommend mass testing.

q/d-when.n: When is the best time to take vitamin D?
q/d-when.a: With the fattiest meal of the day, because it is fat-soluble and better absorbed. The time of day matters less than consistency.

i/akkermansia.sum: A gut bacterium linked with better metabolism. Sold as a "next-generation" probiotic.
b: One small study with pasteurised bacteria
i/akkermansia.w: Generally safe in studies. Caution if your immune system is suppressed.

i/beefliver.sum: Dried liver in capsules, a source of vitamin A, B12, iron and copper.
f: Check the vitamin A per dose
i/beefliver.w: A lot of vitamin A: avoid in pregnancy and with other vitamin A supplements. Avoid with haemochromatosis, thalassaemia and Wilson's disease.

i/betacarotene.sum: An orange pigment the body turns into vitamin A as needed.
b: A safe source of vitamin A from food
f: Supplements do not prevent cancer or heart disease
fd: Carrot, sweet potato, pumpkin, spinach, apricot
i/betacarotene.w: Supplements increase lung cancer in smokers and people exposed to asbestos (ATBC and CARET trials). High intake harmlessly turns the skin yellow.

i/chaga.sum: A fungus that grows on birch trees. Drunk as a tea or extract.
b: Lab studies only, not in humans
i/chaga.w: Very high in oxalates: kidney damage has been reported with long-term use. Caution with anticoagulants and diabetes medicines.

i/chlorophyll.sum: The green pigment of plants. Supplements contain chlorophyllin, a semi-synthetic form.
i/chlorophyll.w: Green stools and tongue. May increase sensitivity to the sun.

i/garlicext.sum: Garlic supplements, usually aged garlic extract or powder.
b: Small drop in blood pressure in hypertension
i/garlicext.w: Increases bleeding risk with anticoagulants and before surgery. Reduces the effect of HIV medicines. Garlic breath.

i/lysine.sum: An essential amino acid. Sold mainly for cold sores.
b: Conflicting small studies, perhaps only at 3 g/day or more
i/lysine.w: Generally safe. Avoid with kidney disease. Antiviral medicines are the proven treatment for cold sores.

i/mullein.sum: A herb with soft, hairy leaves, drunk as a tea for coughs.
b: Ear infection pain, in drops with other herbs
i/mullein.w: The fine hairs irritate the throat if not strained well. No ear drops if the eardrum may be perforated.

i/nettle.sum: The leaves and the root are used for different purposes.
b: Urinary symptoms in benign prostate enlargement (root)
fd: Cooked nettles in pies and soups
i/nettle.w: May affect blood sugar, blood pressure, lithium and anticoagulants. Avoid in pregnancy.

i/plantprotein.sum: Protein from pea, rice or soy, for people who do not eat dairy.
b: Muscle mass with training, similar to whey at an adequate dose
Meeting protein needs on a vegan diet
f: Together they provide all essential amino acids
i/plantprotein.w: Choose products certified for heavy metals. Caution with kidney disease.

i/seamoss.sum: A red seaweed sold as a gel or capsules, often marketed as "nature's multivitamin".
i/seamoss.w: Too much iodine can upset the thyroid. Possible heavy metals. Caution with Hashimoto's and in pregnancy.

i/shilajit.sum: A resin-like substance from Himalayan rocks, rich in fulvic acid.
f: Only standardised and tested for metals
i/shilajit.w: RISK of heavy metals (lead, arsenic) in unprocessed products. Avoid in pregnancy, gout and haemochromatosis.

i/haircomplex.sum: Combinations of millet extract, L-cystine, keratin and B vitamins, sold for hair loss.
b: Telogen hair shedding (after stress, illness or childbirth)
i/haircomplex.w: Hair loss is often caused by iron deficiency, thyroid problems or hormones: check these first. If it contains biotin, it distorts thyroid and troponin tests.

i/hibiscus.sum: A red, tart tea made from the calyces of the hibiscus flower.
i/hibiscus.w: May lower blood pressure too much together with blood pressure medicines. Interacts with hydrochlorothiazide and paracetamol. Avoid in pregnancy.

i/hydroxytyrosol.sum: A polyphenol from olive oil and olives, with an approved EU health claim.
b: Approved EFSA claim at 5 mg/day from olive oil
i/hydroxytyrosol.w: Generally safe. Prefer olive oil as food.

i/mastic.sum: A resin from the mastic tree of Chios. The European Medicines Agency recognises it as a traditional herbal medicine for mild indigestion.
b: One small Greek study and traditional use
Low eradication in small studies, does not replace antibiotics
fd: Mastic as a spice in sweets and bread
i/mastic.w: Generally safe. Possible allergy in people allergic to pistachios (same plant family). Persistent heartburn needs a doctor.

i/mgspray.n: Magnesium on the skin (spray, oil, Epsom salts)
i/mgspray.sum: Magnesium chloride or sulphate applied to the skin or added to a bath.
b: Meaningful absorption through the skin has not been shown
Small studies, massage may be what helps
fd: Leafy greens, nuts, legumes, whole grains
i/mgspray.w: May sting or irritate the skin. For a deficiency, magnesium by mouth is the evidence-based choice.

i/rosehip.sum: The fruit of the wild rose, with vitamin C and galactolipids.
i/rosehip.w: Generally safe. Caution with kidney stones and anticoagulants.

i/zeolite.w: May bind medicines and nutrients: keep at least 2 hours apart from medicines. Some products contain lead or aluminium. Constipation.

s/urticaria.alert: Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat or difficulty breathing: call emergency services immediately. Chronic hives are treated with antihistamines.
lifex: A diary of possible triggers (heat, pressure, stress)

s/dryskin.alert: Severe dry, itchy skin may be linked to the thyroid, kidneys or eczema.

s/melasma.alert: A new dark spot that changes shape or colour needs a dermatologist.
avoid: Perfume on the skin in the sun
lifex: Broad-spectrum sunscreen every day, even when cloudy

s/bronchitis.alert: High fever, shortness of breath or a cough lasting more than 3 weeks needs a doctor to rule out pneumonia. Antibiotics usually do not help.
lifex: Honey for the cough (not for babies)

s/otitis.alert: In babies, with high fever, swelling behind the ear or fluid from the ear, see a doctor. Many ear infections clear on their own in 2–3 days.
avoid: Herbal ear drops if there is discharge
lifex: Breastfeeding and no smoking at home

s/sciatica.alert: Leg weakness, numbness around the genitals or loss of bladder or bowel control: go to hospital immediately.
diff: Without pain running down the leg

s/frozen_shoulder.alert: Left shoulder pain with chest pain or breathlessness: call emergency services. Frozen shoulder is more common in diabetes.

s/hip_oa.alert: Sudden hip pain after a fall in an older person may be a fracture.

s/fibroids.alert: Very heavy periods, dizziness or pain need a gynaecologist. Anaemia is common.
avoid: High doses of green tea extract without a doctor
why_v: Low levels linked with larger fibroids, small studies
If there is anaemia from heavy periods
One small study, only with a doctor because of the liver

s/vaginal_dryness.alert: Bleeding after menopause needs a gynaecologist. Local oestrogen is safe and very effective.

s/irregular_periods.alert: More than 3 months without a period (when not pregnant) needs a gynaecologist. Take a pregnancy test.
lifex: Weight loss if there is obesity

s/mastalgia.alert: A lump you can feel, or changes in the nipple or skin, need a doctor.
avoid: Reported to worsen it, weak data

s/heartfailure.alert: Weight gain of more than 2 kg in 3 days, breathlessness when lying down or swelling: contact your cardiologist promptly.
why_v: Fewer hospital admissions in one trial (Q-SYMBIO)
Intravenous iron for deficiency, only from a cardiologist

s/homocysteine.alert: Very high values need checking for B12 or folate deficiency, kidney disease or an inherited cause.
avoid: Lowering it did not prevent heart attacks in trials

s/adrenal_fatigue.alert: This is not a recognised diagnosis. True adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease) is serious: weakness, weight loss, low blood pressure and darkened skin need a doctor.
avoid: May contain cortisol or thyroid hormones

s/leaky_gut.alert: Increased permeability occurs in some diseases (coeliac, Crohn's), but it is not a recognised diagnosis on its own. The tests on sale are not reliable.

s/histamine.alert: Diagnosis is difficult and the tests are doubtful. Flushing, headache, diarrhoea or hives after certain foods can have other causes too.
avoid: Very aged cheeses, cured meats, pickles
lifex: Fresh rather than aged foods, with a dietitian

s/hypoglycemia.alert: In people on insulin or sulfonylureas, blood sugar under 70 needs 15 g of sugar immediately. Fainting or confusion: call emergency services.
avoid: Sugar and soft drinks on their own
Cause a sharp rise and fall
lifex: Small meals with protein and fibre

s/hirsutism.alert: Rapid onset, a deepening voice or clitoral enlargement need an urgent endocrine check.
lifex: Weight loss if there is obesity

s/bruising.alert: Unexplained bruises with bleeding gums, nosebleeds or tiny red spots need a blood test. Anticoagulants and aspirin are common causes.

s/cheilitis.n: Cracks at the corners of the mouth
s/cheilitis.alert: Often caused by a fungus or bacteria. If it does not clear, see a doctor.

s/burning_mouth.alert: Check B12, folate, iron, blood sugar and medicines. A sore on the tongue that does not heal in 2 weeks needs a doctor.

s/twitching.alert: Twitching with muscle weakness, difficulty swallowing or muscle wasting needs a neurologist. Most twitching is harmless.
avoid: A lot of caffeine and energy drinks

s/concussion.alert: Repeated vomiting, confusion, weakness, seizures or a worsening headache: go to hospital immediately.
avoid: Returning to sport the same day
lifex: A few days of rest and a gradual return

s/autism.alert: The core support is early intervention (speech, occupational and behavioural therapy). Many online "treatments" are dangerous.
why_v: Folinic acid in a subgroup, only with a doctor

s/gilbert.alert: A harmless inherited condition with slightly raised bilirubin. Yellowing with dark urine, pain or fever needs a doctor.

s/hearing_loss.alert: Sudden hearing loss in one ear is urgent: see an ENT doctor within 72 hours.
why_v: One study in people with low folate

s/myopia_kids.alert: Needs regular eye checks. Treatments exist that slow progression (atropine drops, special glasses).
avoid: A lot of close work without breaks
why_v: Linked, but outdoor light seems to be what matters

s/kids_colds.alert: 6–10 viral infections a year are normal in young children. Difficulty breathing, dehydration or fever lasting more than 3 days need a paediatrician.

s/kids_growth.n: Child who is short or thin
s/kids_growth.alert: The paediatrician assesses the growth curve. A slowing growth rate needs checking.
lifex: A varied diet with protein and dairy

s/cancer_prevention.alert: No supplement has been shown to prevent cancer. Some increase the risk. Screening tests save lives.
why_v: Perhaps fewer cancer deaths, not fewer diagnoses
Nicotinamide for skin cancer at high risk

s/breast_cancer.alert: Tell your oncologist about every supplement: some interact with tamoxifen and aromatase inhibitors.
why_v: For the bones, if diet falls short

s/prostate_cancer.alert: Tell your urologist about every supplement. Hormone therapy causes osteoporosis and muscle loss.
why_v: For the bones during hormone therapy

s/lpa.alert: Lp(a) is mainly inherited. One measurement in a lifetime is enough. If it is high, control the other risk factors more strictly.
avoid: Supplements that promise to lower it
lifex: Controlling LDL, blood pressure and blood sugar
why_v: Lowers it, but no benefit on heart attacks and has side effects

s/ptsd.alert: Treatments with strong evidence: trauma-focused psychotherapy (e.g. EMDR) and medicines. If you have thoughts of self-harm, contact a crisis line or emergency services immediately.

s/mgdef.alert: Common with proton pump inhibitors, diuretics, alcohol and diarrhoea. Very low magnesium causes arrhythmias.
lifex: Nuts, legumes, green vegetables, whole grains

s/hypokalemia.alert: Very low potassium causes weakness and arrhythmias. Replacement with tablets only on medical advice with blood tests.
avoid: Laxatives and diuretics without a doctor
why_v: If magnesium is also low, potassium will not correct

s/hyperpara.alert: In primary hyperparathyroidism calcium is already high: supplements only with an endocrinologist. A common cause of the secondary form is vitamin D deficiency.
why_v: In the secondary form from deficiency, or with caution in the primary form

s/ncgs.alert: Before cutting out gluten, get tested for coeliac disease. After stopping gluten the test gives a false negative.
avoid: A strict gluten-free diet without reason
Less fibre and fewer B vitamins
diff: Fructans, not gluten, are often to blame
lifex: A low-FODMAP diet with a dietitian

s/sarcoidosis.alert: In sarcoidosis vitamin D can raise calcium dangerously. Calcium and vitamin D only on medical advice with blood tests.

q/vitc-iron.n: Does vitamin C help iron absorption?
q/vitc-iron.a: Yes, vitamin C increases the absorption of iron from plant foods and supplements. A glass of orange juice or a pepper with the meal is enough. Recent studies show the extra benefit with iron supplements is small.

q/d-winter.n: Do I need vitamin D in winter?
q/d-winter.a: From November to March the sun in Greece makes little vitamin D, and many people have low levels. People who stay indoors a lot, older adults and people with dark skin benefit from 800–1000 IU a day in winter.

q/d-toxic.n: How much vitamin D is too much?
q/d-toxic.a: The safe upper limit for adults is 4000 IU a day. Toxicity (high calcium, nausea, kidney stones) usually appears with tens of thousands of IU for months or with dosing mistakes. 25(OH)D levels above 100 ng/ml are very high.

q/k2-mk7.a: MK-7 stays longer in the blood and is taken once a day (90–200 µg). MK-4 needs much larger doses. The data on bones and blood vessels are still limited for both. People on warfarin should not take K2 without their doctor.

q/bcomplex-energy.n: Do B vitamins give you energy?
q/bcomplex-energy.a: B vitamins are needed to produce energy, but they only give you energy if you are deficient. In people without a deficiency they do not fix tiredness. Fatigue needs checking for iron, B12, thyroid and sleep.

q/zn-longterm.n: How long can I take zinc?
q/zn-longterm.a: Up to 25–40 mg a day is safe. Higher doses for months cause copper deficiency, with anaemia and nerve damage. For long-term use above 25 mg, choose a product with 1–2 mg of copper.

q/ashwa-thyroid.a: It may raise thyroid hormones. Cases of hyperthyroidism have been reported. People with a thyroid condition or on thyroxine should ask their doctor and check their TSH.

q/mg-sleep.a: The studies are few and small, mostly in older adults. The benefit is small: falling asleep a few minutes faster. It probably helps most in people who are deficient. It is safe to try.

q/collagen-joints.a: Small studies show a small reduction in pain in osteoarthritis and in athletes, but they are often industry-funded. Strengthening exercises and weight loss help much more.

q/creatine-women.a: Yes. Creatine helps strength and muscle in women too, and it is being studied for bones after menopause. It can raise weight slightly because of water in the muscles, not fat. There is not enough data in pregnancy.

q/creatine-brain.a: Small studies show a small improvement in memory, mainly in vegetarians, older adults and during sleep deprivation. The data are still early.

q/coq10-who.a: The body makes its own Q10. It is studied in heart failure, migraine and muscle pain from statins, with small or conflicting benefits. Healthy people do not need it.

q/omega3-afib.a: Yes, at high doses. Meta-analyses show that more than 1 g a day increases the risk of atrial fibrillation by about 25%. People with an arrhythmia should ask their cardiologist.

q/fish-vs-pills.a: Fish is better: besides omega-3 it has protein, vitamin D, selenium and iodine, and it is linked with fewer heart attacks. Capsules are an option for people who do not eat fish. Two portions of oily fish a week are enough.

q/probiotic-daily.n: Should I take a probiotic every day?
q/probiotic-daily.a: Healthy people do not need one. Probiotics have evidence for specific cases, such as diarrhoea from antibiotics and some irritable bowel symptoms. Fibre and fermented foods support the microbiome every day.

q/gummies.a: They are absorbed normally, but they often contain sugar, lower doses and lose potency over time. They look like sweets, so keep them away from children: iron overdose is dangerous.

q/liposomal.a: Small studies show slightly better absorption for some (e.g. vitamin C, glutathione), but no proof of better health outcomes. They cost much more.

q/alcohol-vitamins.a: Regular drinking mainly lowers thiamine (B1), folate, B6, magnesium and zinc. B1 deficiency can seriously damage the brain. The answer is to cut down on alcohol, and in dependence to take B1 on medical advice.

q/vegan-iron.n: How do I get enough iron as a vegan?
q/vegan-iron.a: Legumes, tofu, seeds, nuts and green vegetables, with vitamin C in the same meal. Soaking and sprouting help. Keep tea and coffee away from meals. Check your ferritin once a year.

q/calcium-heart.n: Do calcium supplements harm the heart?
q/calcium-heart.a: Some meta-analyses found a small rise in heart attacks with supplements taken without vitamin D, others did not. Calcium from food does not raise the risk. It is better to get calcium from your diet and supplement only what is missing.

q/vita-pregnancy.n: Why is vitamin A dangerous in pregnancy?
q/vita-pregnancy.a: High doses of retinol (more than 10,000 IU a day) cause birth defects. Avoid supplements with retinol, liver and cod liver oil. Beta-carotene from fruit and vegetables is safe.

q/pregnancy-fish.n: Which fish are safe in pregnancy?
q/pregnancy-fish.a: 2–3 portions a week of low-mercury fish are recommended: sardines, anchovies, salmon, cod, sea bream. Avoid swordfish, shark and large tuna. Raw fish and seafood are best avoided.

q/pregnancy-caffeine.n: How much coffee can I drink in pregnancy?
q/pregnancy-caffeine.a: Up to 200 mg of caffeine a day, about 1–2 cups of filter coffee or 2 espressos. Tea, cola, chocolate and energy drinks count too.

q/kids-d.a: Yes. Breastfed babies need 400 IU a day from the first days until their first birthday. Formula milks already contain vitamin D. Ask your paediatrician about the dose.

q/kids-omega3.a: Children who eat fish 1–2 times a week do not need a supplement. In ADHD the benefit is small. If your child does not eat fish, a children's product is a reasonable choice.

q/kids-iron.n: When does a child need iron?
q/kids-iron.a: Only when tests show a deficiency. At risk are premature babies, babies who drink a lot of cow's milk before age 1, and teenage girls with heavy periods. Iron overdose is one of the most dangerous poisonings in children.

q/elderly-protein.n: How much protein do I need after 65?
q/elderly-protein.a: More than younger people: 1–1.2 g per kilo of body weight a day, spread over 3 meals with 25–30 g each. Together with strength exercises it prevents muscle loss. With kidney disease, only with your doctor.

q/sleep-weekend.n: Can I catch up on sleep at the weekend?
q/sleep-weekend.a: Partly. Extra sleep helps with tiredness, but it does not fully fix the metabolic effects of sleep loss. Big changes in wake-up time disrupt the body clock. A steady schedule is better.

q/walk-after-meal.n: Does walking after a meal help?
q/walk-after-meal.a: Yes. 10–15 minutes of walking after a meal reduces the rise in blood sugar, especially in diabetes. Even 2–5 minutes help.

q/strength-howoften.n: How often should I do weight training?
q/strength-howoften.a: Twice a week for all the major muscle groups is the WHO recommendation. Even 30–60 minutes a week is linked with lower mortality. Start light and increase gradually.

q/weight-loss-speed.n: How fast is it safe to lose weight?
q/weight-loss-speed.a: About 0.5–1 kg a week. Very fast loss increases muscle loss and the risk of gallstones. Very low-calorie diets only with medical supervision.

q/glp1-muscle.n: Do I lose muscle on the new weight loss medicines?
q/glp1-muscle.a: Part of the weight lost (about 25–40%) is lean mass, as with any large weight loss. Enough protein and strength exercises help keep the muscle.

q/late-eating.n: Does eating late at night make you fat?
q/late-eating.a: Total calories matter more. But studies show late meals raise blood sugar more and disturb sleep. It is good to have the last meal 2–3 hours before bed.

q/seed-oils.a: Studies do not show that seed oils harm the heart. When they replace saturated fat they lower cholesterol. They are not suited to repeated frying at high temperatures. Olive oil is the best choice.

q/milk-adults.a: For those who tolerate it, milk and especially yogurt are good sources of protein, calcium and iodine. It is not essential: calcium can come from other foods too. With lactose intolerance, yogurt and hard cheeses are usually tolerated.

q/pink-salt.a: No. It is also almost entirely sodium chloride. Its trace minerals are in very small amounts. It usually has no iodine, while iodised salt helps the thyroid.

q/honey-sugar.a: Only slightly. Honey has some antioxidants, but for the body it is mostly sugar and it raises blood sugar. Use it in moderation. Never for babies under 1 year.

q/dark-chocolate.a: Chocolate with 70% cocoa or more has flavanols that lower blood pressure slightly. But it has many calories: 20–30 g a day is enough. Some products contain cadmium and lead.

q/ginger-nausea.a: Yes, it has good evidence for nausea in pregnancy and after surgery, less for travel sickness. Usually 1 g a day in divided doses. In pregnancy ask your doctor.

q/ferritin-high.a: Ferritin rises with inflammation, fatty liver, alcohol, obesity and iron overload (e.g. haemochromatosis, transfusions). Transferrin saturation also needs measuring. Stop any iron supplement until you are checked.
